official_scope: plant life and general botany principles
design_notes: Expanded all eight locked topics into atomic concepts, varying from 9 to 12 per topic based on testable density. Microscopy and cross-section interpretation are anchored to cell and organ topics; physiology, genetics, ecology, and applied chapters each carry separate lab/calculation or diagnostic concepts where relevant. No topics were renamed or reordered.

topics.title: Plant cells and microscopy
topics.why_this_topic: Students need a foundational chapter for cell organelles, unique plant structures, and microscopy skills before moving to tissues and organs.
topics.scope_note: Includes cell wall, membrane, plastids, vacuole, plasmodesmata, cytoskeleton, and light microscope interpretation; excludes whole-organ anatomy and metabolic pathways.

concepts.title: Plant cell wall structure
concepts.description: Identify layers and components of primary and secondary plant cell walls, including cellulose, hemicellulose, pectin, and lignin.

concepts.title: Cellulose microfibril orientation
concepts.description: Explain how cortical microtubules direct cellulose synthase movement and microfibril deposition, and how orientation influences cell expansion.

concepts.title: Plant cell membrane structure
concepts.description: Identify phospholipid bilayer components, embedded proteins, and selective permeability functions in plant cells.

concepts.title: Plastid types and interconversion
concepts.description: Distinguish chloroplasts, chromoplasts, amyloplasts, and proplastids by structure and function, and explain their developmental relationships.

concepts.title: Chloroplast structure
concepts.description: Identify thylakoid, granum, stroma, inner and outer membranes, and explain compartment roles in photosynthesis.

concepts.title: Central vacuole and turgor pressure
concepts.description: Explain how the central vacuole maintains turgor pressure, stores solutes and pigments, and drives cell expansion.

concepts.title: Plasmodesmata and symplastic transport
concepts.description: Describe plasmodesmata structure and how they connect protoplasts to form the symplast, allowing cell-to-cell trafficking.

concepts.title: Plant cytoskeleton
concepts.description: Identify roles of microtubules and actin filaments in plant cell division, cell wall deposition, cytoplasmic streaming, and organelle movement.

concepts.title: Light microscope interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret plant cell and tissue images obtained by brightfield microscopy, including identifying organelles, cell types, and section planes.

concepts.title: Microscope measurement and scale
concepts.description: Calculate actual cell or tissue sizes from field-of-view diameter and micrometer scales, and convert between magnification levels.

topics.title: Plant organs and development
topics.why_this_topic: Roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and spore-forming bodies are the structural vocabulary tested together with growth and differentiation, so they form one anatomy chapter.
topics.scope_note: Includes primary and secondary meristems, tissue systems, organ cross-sections, spore-forming bodies, growth and differentiation, and woody vs herbaceous habit; excludes cellular organelles and transport physiology.

concepts.title: Apical meristems and primary growth
concepts.description: Identify apical meristem zones and explain how primary meristems produce dermal, ground, and vascular tissues.

concepts.title: Vascular cambium and cork cambium
concepts.description: Distinguish vascular cambium and cork cambium, and describe their roles in secondary growth in woody plants.

concepts.title: Dermal, ground, and vascular tissue systems
concepts.description: Identify the three tissue systems and their main cell types across plant organs.

concepts.title: Root anatomy and cross sections
concepts.description: Identify root regions, tissue layers, and monocot vs dicot root cross-sectional features such as endodermis, pericycle, and vascular arrangement.

concepts.title: Stem anatomy and cross sections
concepts.description: Identify stem cross-sectional features including vascular bundle arrangement in monocot and dicot stems, pith, cortex, and secondary xylem.

concepts.title: Leaf anatomy and cross sections
concepts.description: Identify leaf layers and structures—epidermis, mesophyll, vascular bundles, stomata—and relate them to photosynthesis and gas exchange.

concepts.title: Flower organ structure
concepts.description: Identify sepals, petals, stamens, and carpels, and describe how their arrangement supports pollination and fertilization.

concepts.title: Spore-forming bodies
concepts.description: Recognize sori, sporangia, cones, strobili, and capsules as spore-producing structures across plant groups.

concepts.title: Primary growth and cell differentiation
concepts.description: Explain how apical meristem cells differentiate into specialized cell types and elongate during primary growth.

concepts.title: Secondary growth and wood anatomy
concepts.description: Explain how vascular cambium produces secondary xylem and phloem, leading to wood and bark formation.

concepts.title: Woody vs herbaceous habit
concepts.description: Compare woody and herbaceous plant stems in terms of secondary growth, support, and life cycle.

concepts.title: Modified roots, stems, and leaves
concepts.description: Identify modified organs such as tubers, rhizomes, tendrils, bulbs, and storage roots and explain their functions.

topics.title: Transport, nutrition, and gas exchange
topics.why_this_topic: Water, gas, and mineral movement is a distinct physiology skill set often tested with diagrams and data.
topics.scope_note: Includes xylem and phloem, transpiration, translocation, water potential, stomatal gas exchange, mineral nutrition, and storage of gases and water; excludes photosynthesis biochemistry and pathology.

concepts.title: Water potential components
concepts.description: Calculate water potential from solute and pressure potentials and predict direction of water movement between compartments.

concepts.title: Cohesion-tension theory of transpiration
concepts.description: Explain how transpiration generates tension and pulls water upward through xylem via cohesion and adhesion.

concepts.title: Stomatal regulation of gas exchange
concepts.description: Explain how guard cells regulate stomatal aperture via turgor, ion fluxes, and environmental signals to balance CO2 uptake and water loss.

concepts.title: Xylem structure and water transport
concepts.description: Relate xylem vessel and tracheid structure to water movement, cavitation, and embolism repair.

concepts.title: Phloem translocation and pressure-flow
concepts.description: Apply the pressure-flow hypothesis to explain source-to-sink movement of sugars through sieve tubes and companion cells.

concepts.title: Essential mineral nutrients and deficiency symptoms
concepts.description: Identify essential macro- and micronutrients and diagnose common deficiency symptoms based on mobility and plant growth responses.

concepts.title: Nitrogen uptake and assimilation
concepts.description: Describe how plants take up nitrate and ammonium and assimilate them into amino acids, and contrast with biological nitrogen fixation.

concepts.title: Storage of water and gases in plants
concepts.description: Identify adaptations for water storage (succulence, tubers) and gas storage/transport (aerenchyma, pneumatophores) in plants.

concepts.title: Root pressure and guttation
concepts.description: Explain root pressure generation and conditions that produce guttation, and contrast with transpiration-driven water movement.

topics.title: Photosynthesis and plant biochemistry
topics.why_this_topic: Photosynthesis and general plant biochemistry are core chemical processes assessed separately from structural anatomy.
topics.scope_note: Includes light reactions, Calvin cycle, C3/C4/CAM pathways, pigments, respiration, primary metabolites, and secondary metabolites; excludes cell anatomy and transport.

concepts.title: Photosynthetic pigments and absorption spectra
concepts.description: Identify chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, carotenoids, and phycobilins and interpret absorption and action spectra.

concepts.title: Light reactions and electron transport
concepts.description: Describe how photosystem II and I drive electron transport, split water, and produce NADPH and ATP during linear electron flow.

concepts.title: Photophosphorylation
concepts.description: Explain how the thylakoid proton gradient powers ATP synthase to produce ATP in chloroplasts.

concepts.title: Calvin cycle carbon fixation
concepts.description: Outline the three phases of the Calvin cycle—carboxylation, reduction, regeneration—and identify inputs, outputs, and key enzymes.

concepts.title: Rubisco and photorespiration
concepts.description: Explain Rubisco oxygenase activity, photorespiration, and its costs in C3 plants under high temperature and low CO2.

concepts.title: C4 carbon fixation pathway
concepts.description: Compare C4 pathway spatial separation of carbon fixation in mesophyll and bundle sheath cells and its advantage under heat and drought.

concepts.title: CAM photosynthesis
concepts.description: Explain how CAM plants temporally separate CO2 fixation and Calvin cycle using nocturnal acid accumulation and daytime decarboxylation.

concepts.title: Plant cellular respiration
concepts.description: Describe glycolysis, citric acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation in plant mitochondria and how respiration supplies ATP and carbon skeletons.

concepts.title: Primary plant metabolites
concepts.description: Identify major primary metabolites—carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids—and their roles in plant structure and metabolism.

concepts.title: Secondary plant metabolites
concepts.description: Classify major secondary metabolites (alkaloids, terpenoids, phenolics) and describe their ecological and pharmacological functions.

concepts.title: Plant pigment chromatography
concepts.description: Separate and identify plant pigments by paper or thin-layer chromatography and calculate Rf values.

topics.title: Reproduction and plant genetics
topics.why_this_topic: Reproduction and genetics require a dedicated chapter because they combine life cycles, Mendelian principles, and modern biotechnology.
topics.scope_note: Includes alternation of generations, flower, fruit, seed, and spore reproduction, basic plant genetics, polyploidy, and GMOs; excludes taxonomic classification and ecology.

concepts.title: Alternation of generations
concepts.description: Describe the alternation between multicellular gametophyte and sporophyte generations and identify ploidy transitions.

concepts.title: Gametophyte vs sporophyte dominance
concepts.description: Compare life cycles of bryophytes, ferns, gymnosperms, and angiosperms in terms of dominant generation and gametophyte independence.

concepts.title: Angiosperm sexual reproduction
concepts.description: Trace male and female gametophyte development in flowers, from microsporogenesis and megasporogenesis to mature pollen and embryo sac.

concepts.title: Pollination and double fertilization
concepts.description: Distinguish pollination mechanisms and explain double fertilization leading to zygote and endosperm formation in angiosperms.

concepts.title: Seed structure and germination
concepts.description: Identify seed coat, embryo, cotyledons, and endosperm, and explain germination requirements including water, oxygen, and temperature.

concepts.title: Fruit types and seed dispersal
concepts.description: Classify simple, aggregate, and multiple fruits and relate fruit structure to seed dispersal mechanisms.

concepts.title: Asexual reproduction and vegetative propagation
concepts.description: Describe natural and artificial vegetative propagation methods including runners, cuttings, grafting, and tissue culture.

concepts.title: Spore reproduction in non-seed plants
concepts.description: Outline spore production and dispersal in mosses and ferns, including gametophyte development from spores.

concepts.title: Mendelian genetics in plants
concepts.description: Apply Punnett squares, dominance, segregation, and independent assortment to plant crosses and predict phenotypic ratios.

concepts.title: Polyploidy in plants
concepts.description: Explain how polyploidy arises and how it influences plant fertility, gene expression, and crop improvement.

concepts.title: Plant biotechnology and GMOs
concepts.description: Describe genetic modification techniques used in plants, including Agrobacterium-mediated transformation and CRISPR, and evaluate GMO applications.

topics.title: Plant diversity, evolution, and history
topics.why_this_topic: The rules require major taxonomic groups, evolutionary history, and distinguishing group comparisons, which form a cohesive biodiversity chapter.
topics.scope_note: Includes algae vs multicellular plants, embryophytes vs cryptogams, monocot vs dicot, major taxonomic groups, paleobotany, plant evolution, history of botany, and importance of plant diversity; excludes ecological interactions and human uses.

concepts.title: Algae vs multicellular plants
concepts.description: Distinguish algae from multicellular embryophytes based on structure, reproduction, alternation of generations, and adaptations to land.

concepts.title: Embryophytes vs cryptogams
concepts.description: Contrast embryophytes (land plants with embryos) with cryptogams (seedless plants) and identify which groups belong to each.

concepts.title: Bryophyte characteristics and life cycle
concepts.description: Identify mosses, liverworts, and hornworts by structure and describe their dominant gametophyte life cycle.

concepts.title: Seedless vascular plants
concepts.description: Identify ferns, club mosses, horsetails, and whisk ferns and describe vascular tissue and spore-based reproduction.

concepts.title: Gymnosperms and seed evolution
concepts.description: Identify conifers, cycads, ginkgo, and gnetophytes and explain pollen and naked-seed adaptations.

concepts.title: Angiosperm evolution and flower/fruit innovation
concepts.description: Explain how flowers and fruits distinguish angiosperms and contributed to their diversification and coevolution with pollinators and dispersers.

concepts.title: Monocot vs dicot comparison
concepts.description: Compare monocot and dicot (eudicot) embryos, leaf venation, vascular bundle arrangement, root structure, floral parts, and pollen apertures.

concepts.title: Plant evolutionary history and paleobotany
concepts.description: Outline major events in plant evolution from green algae to land plants to angiosperms using fossil evidence and phylogeny.

concepts.title: Paleobotany and fossil interpretation
concepts.description: Identify plant fossil types (compressions, impressions, permineralizations, casts) and infer ancient environments from fossil assemblages.

concepts.title: History of botany and key figures
concepts.description: Identify contributions of major botanists such as Theophrastus, Linnaeus, Mendel, Hooke, Darwin, and modern plant scientists.

concepts.title: Major plant taxonomic groups and classification
concepts.description: Place major plant groups within a modern phylogenetic classification and use botanical names to identify family, genus, and species relationships.

topics.title: Plant ecology and global cycles
topics.why_this_topic: Plants in cycles and communities is an ecology chapter that links plant physiology to ecosystem function.
topics.scope_note: Includes plants in global energy and nutrient cycles, carbon, nitrogen, and water cycling, competition in plant communities, succession, and symbiosis; excludes agriculture, economic uses, and disease.

concepts.title: Plants in the global carbon cycle
concepts.description: Explain how photosynthesis fixes carbon and respiration/decomposition release it, and how plant biomass acts as a carbon sink.

concepts.title: Plants in the nitrogen cycle
concepts.description: Trace nitrogen transformations (fixation, nitrification, uptake, decomposition) and identify plant roles and nitrogen limitations.

concepts.title: Plants in the water cycle
concepts.description: Explain how transpiration and canopy interception influence precipitation, runoff, and soil moisture in the hydrologic cycle.

concepts.title: Primary productivity and energy flow
concepts.description: Measure gross and net primary productivity and explain plant role as primary producers in ecosystem energy flow.

concepts.title: Plant competition and community structure
concepts.description: Explain competition for light, water, nutrients, and space and how it shapes plant community composition and zonation.

concepts.title: Ecological succession and plant roles
concepts.description: Distinguish primary and secondary succession and identify pioneer and climax plant communities through seral stages.

concepts.title: Mycorrhizal symbiosis
concepts.description: Distinguish arbuscular and ectomycorrhizae and explain how mycorrhizal fungi enhance plant water and nutrient uptake.

concepts.title: Nitrogen-fixing plant symbiosis
concepts.description: Explain how legumes and actinorhizal plants form nodules with nitrogen-fixing bacteria and how symbiosis supplies nitrogen to ecosystems.

concepts.title: Biomes and plant adaptations
concepts.description: Relate major terrestrial biomes to characteristic plant growth forms and adaptations to climate, fire, and soils.

concepts.title: Plants as ecosystem engineers
concepts.description: Explain how plants modify their environment through shade, litter, soil stabilization, and hydrology, influencing other organisms.

topics.title: Applied plant science and human use
topics.why_this_topic: The rules' applied plant science bullet points—food, medicine, agriculture, disease, and environmental management—are best merged into one human-use chapter to avoid many one-bullet topics.
topics.scope_note: Includes plant products, foodstuffs, horticulture, aquaculture, plants in medicine and environmental management, use of plant materials by animals and humans, and plant diseases including nutrient deficiencies and infections; excludes wild ecology, taxonomy, and basic genetics.

concepts.title: Major food crops and plant foodstuffs
concepts.description: Identify major cereal, legume, root, fruit, and oil crops and the plant parts used for human food.

concepts.title: Plants in medicine
concepts.description: Identify medicinal plants and their active secondary metabolites, and distinguish traditional, herbal, and pharmaceutical uses.

concepts.title: Horticultural practices and crop management
concepts.description: Apply horticultural practices including pruning, training, irrigation, fertilization, and greenhouse management to optimize crop growth.

concepts.title: Aquaculture and aquatic plants
concepts.description: Identify cultivated aquatic plants and explain their roles in aquaculture systems for food, water quality, and habitat.

concepts.title: Plants in environmental management
concepts.description: Explain how plants are used for phytoremediation, erosion control, carbon sequestration, and restoration of degraded ecosystems.

concepts.title: Plant diseases and pathogens
concepts.description: Diagnose fungal, bacterial, viral, and oomycete plant diseases by symptoms, signs, and causal agents.

concepts.title: Plant nutrient deficiency diagnosis
concepts.description: Diagnose nutrient deficiencies from leaf chlorosis, necrosis, and growth patterns, and recommend corrective fertilization.

concepts.title: Economic plant products and materials
concepts.description: Identify plant sources of fibers, wood, oils, resins, rubber, dyes, and beverages and their processing.

concepts.title: Use of plant materials by animals and humans
concepts.description: Describe how animals and humans use plants for shelter, tools, forage, bedding, and cultural purposes beyond food and medicine.

concepts.title: Plant disease management and control
concepts.description: Apply integrated pest management and cultural, biological, chemical, and resistant-variety strategies to manage plant diseases.

concepts.title: Invasive plants and agricultural weeds
concepts.description: Identify invasive plant and weed species and explain their impacts on agriculture, native ecosystems, and management strategies.
